title: California fish larvae had a short-term thermal slope near half their spatial slope in 2000-2020
abstract: We compared spatial and temporal thermal slopes in 2,583 selected CalCOFI fish-larva tows at 45 stations in 2000-2020. Taxon scores were fixed from 1978-1999 records. The short-term slope was 0.1317 index C per water C and the spatial slope was 0.2661. Their ratio was 0.495, with a 95% three-year block interval of 0.439-0.578 and a joint station/year interval of 0.410-0.607. Salinity in both models raised the point ratio to 0.653 because it reduced the spatial slope more than the temporal slope. The short-term result held without 2014-2016 and under other index and sampling choices. The secular ratio had a point value of 0.630, but the water-temperature trend interval crossed zero with serial dependence. A direct test did not resolve a secular deficit relative to full spatial expectation. Thus this second marine survey had a partial short-term response, but did not establish a precise decadal transfer fraction. Local fitted scores, observation effects, 21 years and uncertain processes limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and resample statistics are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Annual adjusted anomalies and short-term/spatial slope ratios. Bars are 95% three-year block intervals conditional on fixed scores and stations. The secular ratio is unstable because its warming denominator is uncertain.
